artifact_chat.scope: 799 historical inventory rows from all 22 pages of NASA’s July 5, 2012 lunar catalogue, plus six retired/lost Mars mission records. Rows can be assemblies, parts, debris or uncertain locations; they are not a count of distinct physical objects. Not a live condition or coordinate survey.

wider_search.note: Optional user-initiated, key-free NASA library search restricted to a selected documented left-behind/retired/lost artifact. Queries contain only its name, mission and world; results must match the artifact and mission. Unknown and unrelated prompts never trigger broad search. collectionSurveyor1.title: Surveyor 1 mission record
collectionSurveyor1.summary: Surveyor 1 landed June 2, 1966. Its primary mission ended July 14, 1966; contact continued until January 7, 1967. The lander stayed on the Moon.

collectionSurveyor5.title: Surveyor 5 mission record
collectionSurveyor5.summary: Surveyor 5 landed September 11, 1967. Contact was lost December 16, 1967, after a mission that returned images and lunar soil chemistry measurements.

collectionSurveyor6.title: Surveyor 6 mission record
collectionSurveyor6.summary: Surveyor 6 landed November 10, 1967, hopped on November 17, and entered hibernation later that month. Contact was briefly recovered December 14, 1967.

collectionSurveyor7.title: Surveyor 7 mission record
collectionSurveyor7.summary: Surveyor 7 landed January 10, 1968, north of Tycho crater. Its final working period ended February 21, 1968.

collectionFalcon.title: Falcon descent stage mission record
collectionFalcon.summary: Apollo 15’s Falcon landed July 30, 1971. Its ascent stage departed August 2 with David Scott and James Irwin. Only the descent stage remained at the landing site.

collectionViking2.title: Viking 2 mission record
collectionViking2.summary: Viking 2 landed September 3, 1976. The surface lander stopped transmitting in April 1980; its separate orbiter ended operations in July 1978.

collectionPathfinder.title: Mars Pathfinder mission record
collectionPathfinder.summary: Mars Pathfinder landed July 4, 1997, and returned its final data September 27, 1997. The lander and Sojourner are separate pieces of hardware left in Ares Vallis.

collectionSojourner.title: Sojourner mission record
collectionSojourner.summary: Sojourner was delivered July 4, 1997. Pathfinder’s final transmission was September 27, 1997, ending the documented joint surface mission. Sojourner remains a separate rover near its lander.

collectionIngenuity.title: Ingenuity mission record
collectionIngenuity.summary: Ingenuity completed 72 flights. Its final flight was January 18, 2024; NASA announced the end of its flight mission January 25 after rotor damage. Flight retirement does not mean every electronic system immediately stopped.

collectionPolarlander.title: Mars Polar Lander mission record
collectionPolarlander.summary: Mars Polar Lander was lost during arrival on December 3, 1999. Contact attempts ended January 17, 2000. Its exact resting location is unconfirmed; planned surface science was not achieved.

collectionMplTarget.title: Mars Polar Lander target region
collectionMplTarget.summary: The intended target was near 76 degrees south and 195 degrees west. These target-area coordinates do not identify a confirmed wreck.

collectionIngenuityAirfield.title: Ingenuity at its final airfield
collectionIngenuityAirfield.summary: A February 2024 rover mosaic shows Ingenuity at its final airfield, nicknamed Valinor Hills. The image is a dated observation, not a live view.

collectionApollo15Details.title: Apollo 15 mission details
collectionApollo15Details.summary: Apollo 15 used Falcon for surface exploration at Hadley-Apennine. Its ascent stage lifted the crew away August 2, 1971; the descent stage stayed at the site.

collectionPathfinderLocation.title: Mars Pathfinder historical landing record
collectionPathfinderLocation.summary: A historical account places the airbag-cushioned landing in Ares Vallis near 19.13 degrees north, 33.22 degrees west. Mapping systems give slightly different coordinates.

collectionSurveyorProgram.title: NASA Ranger and Surveyor programs
collectionSurveyorProgram.summary: Five successful Surveyors performed robotic soft landings, photography and instrument operations before Apollo. Hardware and objectives varied among missions.

surface_expeditions.credit: Original deterministic Three.js regolith, rocks, terrain and compact educational arrangement. Artifacts brought together for exploration; not a real walking route or surveyed model of the Moon or Mars. Model sizes and terrain illustrative. Mars Polar Lander remains unlocated; displayed as its planned design.

story_archive_media.background: 20-second NASA LRO-derived lunar visualization, with matched NASA-source still poster. Original source audio removed. Not a live camera view.
story_archive_media.note: Historical capture dates, image credits, intended-design annotations and primary source URLs accompany each asset. Galleries preserve full frames; InSight deployment and Mars Polar Lander target media are explicitly labelled as intended/design visualizations.
